screening_decisions.reason: Study focuses on ulcerative colitis disease experience rather than chronic non-cancer pain specifically. While UC can cause pain, the study examines broader HRQoL and symptoms including bowel movements, diarrhea, etc. Not focused on chronic pain as primary outcome.

Study focuses on atopic dermatitis (skin condition) with pruritus/itching as main symptom. While pain is mentioned, the primary focus is on dermatologic disease experience, not chronic non-cancer pain.

Study explores parents caring for children with progressive life-threatening illness during complex chronic phase. Does not specifically focus on chronic non-cancer pain; focuses on general caregiving experience.
Study is about pediatric hearing screening program in rural India. Completely unrelated to chronic non-cancer pain in children.

Study involves children with juvenile inflammatory arthritis (chronic pain condition). Uses semi-structured group discussions and patient focus groups (qualitative elements). Explores children's experiences with pain and motivation. Age range appropriate (children with JIA).

Qualitative study examining pain assessment in children with intellectual disabilities. Uses semi-directive interviews to assess autobiographical memory related to pain. Focuses on children's ability to describe pain experiences. Age range 13-20 years (some overlap with target population).

Qualitative study with semistructured interviews with families of children with epidermolysis bullosa (rare genetic blistering-skin disorder with chronic progression). Key theme includes 'the child suffering pain'. Explores parental experiences related to child's chronic pain condition.

Qualitative observational study of parent-adolescent dyads seeking treatment for chronic pain. Uses modified grounded theory to analyze verbal and non-verbal behaviours. Directly addresses chronic pain in children/adolescents and family experience.

Qualitative study using interviews with music therapists with adolescents (13-21 years) with sickle cell disease. SCD causes chronic pain. Study explores how music helps with pain relief and coping. Focuses on pain experience and management strategies.

Study focuses on nurse burnout, not on children/families' experiences of chronic pain. While it involves youth with chronic pain, the perspective is from healthcare providers, not patients or families.

Qualitative study using focus groups and individual interviews with adolescents and parents regarding medically unexplained symptoms (MUS). MUS often includes chronic pain conditions. Explores healthcare perceptions and experiences relevant to chronic pain management.

Qualitative exploratory study with 22 youngsters aged 5-17 years exploring their perception of physiological pain at home/family setting. Uses semidirected interviews and thematic analysis. Directly addresses children's pain experiences and self-management.

Mixed-methods study investigating participant engagement in psychological intervention for youth with functional abdominal pain disorders (FAPD). Includes thematic analysis of qualitative data. FAPD is a chronic non-cancer pain condition. Explores treatment experiences.
Review article about public engagement strategies in global health. Not about children with chronic pain. Completely unrelated to review topic.

Qualitative study about mothers caring for children with atopic eczema. Eczema is primarily a skin condition with itching, not chronic pain. Focus is on maternal role and work generated by disease, not pain experience.

Study focuses on women aged 10-40 years with severe dysmenorrhea. While some participants may be adolescents, the study includes adult women and focuses on menstrual pain in women, not specifically children 3 months-18 years with chronic non-cancer pain.

Qualitative study using grounded theory with fathers of adolescents diagnosed with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA). JIA is a chronic pain condition. Explores father's experience of having a child with chronic pain condition.

Pilot study evaluating cognitive-behavioural training program for adolescents (14-18 years) with chronic non-organic pain. Includes qualitative feedback from adolescents and parents about the program. Directly addresses chronic pain in adolescents.

Qualitative study using focus groups with young people (aged 8-15) and parents of children with sickle cell disease (SCD). SCD causes chronic pain. Explores healthcare experiences and care delivery for children with chronic pain condition.
Methodological guidance paper about applying GRADE-CERQual to qualitative evidence synthesis. Not a primary qualitative study about children with chronic pain.

Qualitative study using focus groups with adolescents (ages 12-17) with chronic pain conditions. Explores pain-related stigma and concealment as coping strategy. Directly addresses adolescent chronic pain experience.
Methodological paper about using PROGRESS acronym for equity lens in systematic reviews. Not a primary qualitative study about children with chronic pain.

Descriptive qualitative study using in-depth interviews with six adolescents with sickle cell disease. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores lived experiences, coping strategies, and social support related to chronic condition.

Descriptive qualitative study with 39 adolescents and young adults (ages 16-24 years) with primary dysmenorrhoea. Some participants fall within target age range (up to 18). Explores pain impacts and coping mechanisms. Dysmenorrhoea is a form of chronic pain.
Conversation and discourse analysis of medical visits involving children with ASD. Focus is on communication patterns in healthcare encounters, not on chronic pain experiences.

Descriptive exploratory qualitative study with children and adolescents who reported chronic postsurgical pain after inguinal herniorrhaphy. Uses semi-structured interviews and content analysis. Directly addresses chronic pain in children.

Qualitative longitudinal descriptive study with children with MS (n=28). MS can cause chronic pain. Uses motivational interviewing sessions and inductive content analysis. Explores barriers and facilitators to medication adherence in youth with chronic condition.

Qualitative study using individual semistructured interviews with 12 adolescents (aged 12-17) with varying forms of chronic pain attending outpatient pain clinic. Uses critical realist thematic analysis. Directly addresses adolescent chronic pain beliefs and experiences.

Qualitative study with seven families of children diagnosed with OI type 1. Pain and fractures identified as most challenging situations. Uses in-depth semistructured interviews and qualitative discourse analysis. Explores family experience with chronic pain condition.

Qualitative study using in-depth interviews with 22 children (6-17 years) with Juvenile Chronic Arthritis. Uses grounded theory method. Examines children's perspectives on coping with chronic pain in daily life.
Quantitative cost-of-illness study assessing economic burden of chronic pain in adolescents. Uses validated measures and calculations, not qualitative methodology exploring experiences/perceptions.

Qualitative study with adolescents using individual semi-structured interviews (n=25) and focus groups (n=11). Explores self-management of arthritis (chronic pain condition). Uses iterative thematic analysis.

Mixed-methods feasibility study of online intervention for children with functional abdominal pain and families. Includes qualitative interviews with families about impressions. FAPD is chronic non-cancer pain condition.

Feasibility evaluation of group therapy intervention for adolescents with chronic idiopathic musculoskeletal pain. Includes semi-structured interviews with healthcare professionals and free text comments from adolescents/parents analyzed using thematic analyses.

Pilot implementation study of psychoeducational intervention for children/adolescents with SCD pain. Includes qualitative feedback gathered to evaluate feasibility and acceptability. SCD causes chronic pain.

Qualitative descriptive study with 44 hospitalized children (4-11 years) describing painful events. Uses qualitative child interviews and inductive content analysis. Explores children's pain experiences directly.

Qualitative follow-up study with parents of children with functional abdominal pain. Uses interviews with open questions and descriptive content analysis. FAPD is chronic non-cancer pain condition. Explores family experience over time.
Theoretical review paper discussing pain theories and familial factors. Not a primary qualitative study collecting data from children/families about their pain experiences.
Methodological paper about cluster searching techniques for systematic reviews. Not a primary qualitative study about children with chronic pain.

Multi-method study developing e-book for parents with child with pediatric chronic pain. Includes qualitative interviews to compile parents' narratives and qualitative data analysis. Directly addresses pediatric chronic pain family experience.

Qualitative interpretative phenomenological analysis with 21 mothers of children living with chronic pain. Uses focus group interviews. Explores parental appraisals of injustice in context of child's chronic pain.

Qualitative study with female patients (mean age 37.4 years, range 15-49) with SLE. While some may be adolescents, majority are adults. Focus is on reproductive health, not specifically chronic pain in children 3 months-18 years.
Methodological guidance paper from Cochrane about qualitative evidence synthesis methods. Not a primary qualitative study about children with chronic pain.

Qualitative study with young people (16-25 years) and adults (26-31 years) with JIA. Some participants fall within target age range (16-18). Uses semistructured interviews and focus groups with thematic analysis. JIA is chronic pain condition.

Qualitative study examining hospitalized children's thematic drawings of pain. Compares hospitalized children with healthy controls. Explores how children express pain through drawings. Addresses children's pain experiences.

Qualitative study with children and adolescents under palliative care. Palliative care typically indicates life-limiting/life-threatening conditions, which may include cancer. Review specifies chronic NON-CANCER pain.
Systematic review examining prevalence rates of chronic pain in children. Quantitative meta-analysis approach, not primary qualitative study exploring experiences/perceptions.
Cochrane review background statement about psychological therapies for parents. Not a primary qualitative study about children's chronic pain experiences.

Mixed-methods study with 53 parents of children aged 7-13 with sickle cell disease. Includes qualitative methods examining relationships between coping and health care utilization. SCD causes chronic pain.

Ethnographic study examining family caregivers' perceptions of comfort measures for children with vaso-occlusive episodes of SCD. Uses interviews conducted in hospital. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores family experience with pain management.
Qualitative study with Aboriginal carers of children with disability. Focus is on intersectionality and provider interactions, not specifically on chronic non-cancer pain experiences.

Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 27 parents of 20 families with chronically ill child. Explores parents' information needs and communication experiences. May include children with chronic pain conditions.

Descriptive qualitative study with young adults (18-25 years) who received chronic pain care in pediatric setting. Uses semistructured interviews and inductive content analysis. Addresses transition experience for those with chronic pain history.

Secondary data analysis with qualitative identification of concerns from individuals with NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas. Includes 31 children, adolescents, and adults. Pain is one of the symptom categories explored. Some participants in target age range.

Mixed-methods study with 14-21-year-olds with rheumatologic diseases. Includes post-participation video interviews with thematic analysis. Rheumatologic illnesses often involve chronic pain. Some participants in target age range (14-18).
Qualitative study about fibromyalgia/chronic pain without organic cause. Focus is on gender models and adult life development. Appears to focus on adult women, not children 3 months-18 years.

Qualitative analysis of social media posts from adolescent SJIA patients (aged 13-20 years) and their parents. SJIA is chronic pain condition. Explores diagnostic experiences and disease impact. Some participants in target age range.

Qualitative study developing PedsQL SCD Module using multiphase qualitative methodology. Includes individual in-depth interviews with 13 pediatric patients ages 5-18 and 18 parents. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores patient/parent perspectives.

Qualitative study with children (age 10-17 years) with physical disabilities about physical activity participation. Focus is on socialization and identity, not specifically on chronic pain experiences.

Qualitative study about parents' perceptions of living with child with chronic liver disease. While pain is mentioned as one theme, primary focus is on liver disease experience, not chronic pain specifically.

Qualitative study with 18 patient-guardian dyads at infusion center for IBD. Uses semistructured interviews and constant comparative method. IBD can cause chronic pain. Explores challenges and coping mechanisms.
Qualitative study using story theory framework with 8 adolescents experiencing headaches. Headache is a form of chronic pain. Explores dimensions of health challenge and approaches to resolution.
Review article providing overview of psychosocial factors in pediatric pain. Not a primary qualitative study collecting new data from children/families.
Abstract appears to contain legal text unrelated to study content. Cannot determine if this is relevant qualitative study about children with chronic pain.

Mixed-methods three-year follow-up study with adolescents (aged 12-18 years) with chronic pain of no known organic cause. Includes interviews showing pain became part of daily life. Directly addresses adolescent chronic pain experience.

Qualitative descriptive study with 8 children (6-8 years) examining words and meaning when describing pain experiences. Uses semistructured interviews and drawings. Directly explores children's pain communication.

Qualitative study using participatory workshops with children, adolescents, and young adults with JIA and parents. Uses qualitative content analysis. JIA is chronic pain condition. Explores healthcare encounter experiences.

Exploratory study gathering information from parents of 43 children (ages 7-16 years) referred for psychological management of chronic pain. Uses questionnaires about child's pain experience and impact. Addresses family experience with chronic pain.

Qualitative descriptive study using semi-structured interviews with 40 hospitalized youth (10-17 years). Explores pain experience, treatment expectations, and assessment tool preferences. Directly addresses youth pain experiences.
Concept analysis of pain in children's drawings and dialogs. Examines how children describe/draw painful experiences. Addresses characteristics of pain concept from children's perspective.

Mixed-method research with four phases including qualitative interviews with children to develop grounded theory of growing pains. Growing pains are a form of recurrent childhood pain. Explores children's experiences.

Qualitative study with eight patients with NSCLBP about exercise prescription and decision making. Abstract does not specify age, but NSCLBP typically affects adults. No indication this is about children 3 months-18 years.

Interpretive phenomenological study exploring experience of living with migraines in six adolescents (ages 12-17 years). Migraine is chronic pain condition. Explores physical and psychological disruptions.

Qualitative study using semistructured interviews with 10 children undergoing chronic transfusion therapy for SCD. Pain is one of five themes emerged. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores child's perspective on QoL.

Co-produced longitudinal qualitative study with 48 young people with SCD aged 13-21 years (mean age 16.6). Many participants in target age range. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores healthcare experiences during transition.

Qualitative study with seven families including children aged 3-6 years in inpatient unit. Focus is on family experience during disease process and hospitalization, not specifically on chronic non-cancer pain.

Qualitative study with 30 children with sickle cell disease asked to make drawings of themselves and themselves in pain. Includes interviews on pain incidence and control. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores children's pain perception.

Qualitative study with 56 participants including parents of children affected with OI. OI causes chronic pain and fractures. Uses semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Explores day-to-day experiences and psychosocial impact.

Qualitative study with seven face-to-face interviews about SCD pain experience. Abstract does not specify age of participants, but given the depth of reflection required, likely includes adults. Cannot confirm children 3 months-18 years.

Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews and focus groups with adolescent patients aged 12-18 years and parents of pediatric patients with SCD hospitalized for VOC. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores pain management experiences.
Qualitative study with in-depth interviews with 15 parents of children diagnosed with recurrent abdominal pain. RAPP is a form of chronic non-cancer pain. Explores parental cognitions and worries.

Multi-methods qualitative study with nine adolescents (aged 12-22 years, mean 15.7) with chronic pain. Includes interviews and monthly diaries analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Directly addresses adolescent chronic pain experience.

Grounded theory study with six teenage girls (14-17 years) with chronic arthritis plus additional interviews. Uses tape-recorded open interviews and diary writing. Chronic arthritis causes chronic pain.

Qualitative study using focus groups with 12 African American families including adolescents with SCD, siblings, and parents. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores family communication about chronic condition.
Qualitative study with 10 two-parent families of children with juvenile arthritis. Explores parents' experience learning to manage child's illness. JIA is chronic pain condition.

Qualitative study with interviews among 39 children with juvenile chronic arthritis in two age groups (6-11 and 12-17 years). Explores children's perception of joint sensations and pain. JCA is chronic pain condition.
Photovoice pilot study with youth living with sickle cell disease. Youth reflect on experiences with SCD using adapted SHOWeD method. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores lived experience.
Abstract appears to contain unrelated text about research ethics in Bolivia. Cannot determine relevance to children with chronic pain in target age range.

Qualitative study with 15 parents of children <18 years and 9 children 12-18 years with SCD receiving CTT. Uses semi-structured interviews and open coding. SCD causes chronic pain. Explores patient and family experience.

Qualitative study interviewing parents of children treated at multidisciplinary chronic pain clinic following initial appointment. Explores parent satisfaction and perceptions of treatment team. Directly addresses pediatric chronic pain care.
Abstract appears to reference mortality statistics from Yorkshire Register of diabetes. Not a qualitative study about chronic pain experiences.

Mixed-methods study developing STPQ questionnaire. Includes focus groups of 28 adolescent and adult patients about content, clarity, relevance. Some participants in target age range (12-18 years). SCD causes chronic pain.

Qualitative study with 10 patients (13-17.5 years) and 9 parents who underwent CBT for pediatric headache. Uses inductive thematic analysis. Migraine is chronic pain condition. Explores treatment experience.
Pre/post design study about insulin delivery decision-making for type 1 diabetes. Not about chronic pain. Diabetes is metabolic condition, not primarily pain-focused.

Qualitative study with individual semi-structured interviews with 22 adolescents (14-18 years) with JIA. Uses open, axial, and selective coding. JIA is chronic pain condition. Explores experiences and perspectives.

Needs assessment study with purposive sample of adolescents (n=23; 14-18 years) from pediatric chronic pain clinics. Includes focus groups and individual interviews with qualitative analysis. Directly addresses adolescent chronic pain needs.
Qualitative study with 44 persons with CRPS about intimacy and relationships. Abstract does not specify age, but CRPS typically affects adults. Cannot confirm children 3 months-18 years.

Qualitative study using focus groups with youth ages 12-17, young adults 18-20, and parents for pediatric IBD. Some participants in target age range. IBD can cause chronic pain. Explores self-management needs.

Qualitative study with 68 parents in pediatric emergency department. Focus is on emergency care dimensions, not specifically on chronic non-cancer pain experiences. Emergency care is acute, not chronic.

N-of-1 trial with 14 children and young people (aged 7-16 years) with JIA and their parents. Includes semistructured interviews about preferences for pain reporting. JIA is chronic pain condition. Explores pain assessment experiences.

Abstract describes a cohort study on infantile spasms and hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, mismatched with title. Not relevant to chronic non-cancer pain experiences.
Focuses on families of children with disabilities/chronic illnesses broadly, not specifically chronic non-cancer pain.
Mixed-methods study with qualitative component exploring functioning limitations and coping strategies in children aged 10-18 with chronic pain.
Qualitative interviews exploring pain experiences in adolescents and adults with CF. Includes adolescent population relevant to the review.
Prospective descriptive quantitative study using pain tools, not qualitative research.
Focuses on recovery after acute femoral fracture, not chronic non-cancer pain.
Quantitative mediation analysis study, not qualitative.
Methodological paper on evidence synthesis, not primary qualitative research on pediatric pain.
Qualitative interviews with children with vasculitis exploring physical, emotional, and social impacts including severe pain.
Methodological paper on theory use in systematic reviews.
Cross-sectional quantitative epidemiological study.
Qualitative interview study with school-aged children exploring their understanding, experiences, and coping with pain.
Focuses on life-limiting conditions broadly, not specifically chronic non-cancer pain.
Qualitative substudy exploring experiences of adolescents with chronic pelvic pain undergoing acupuncture treatment.
Qualitative retrospective interviews exploring adolescent experiences and self-management of longstanding knee pain.
Mixed methods study including qualitative components exploring challenges and coping in children with hEDS and chronic pain symptoms.
Process evaluation with qualitative data exploring adolescents' and parents' opinions on a pain management program.
Cochrane review background section, not primary qualitative research.
Focuses on end-stage renal disease, not chronic non-cancer pain.
Qualitative interviews exploring paternal experiences of parenting an adolescent with chronic pain.
Psychometric validation study, quantitative.
Qualitative systematic review/synthesis, not primary qualitative research.
Qualitative interviews exploring perceptions and impact of a self-management intervention for adolescents with SCD, including pain management.
Qualitative data exploring barriers to treatment adherence including pain management in adolescents with SCD.
Qualitative interviews with adolescents exploring lived experience of pain flares in JIA and chronic idiopathic pain.
Focuses on everyday acute pain from minor injuries/illnesses, not chronic non-cancer pain.
Qualitative focus groups with adolescents with JIA exploring transitional care needs and experiences.
Does not specify pediatric population; likely focuses on adults. Excluded due to unclear age range.
Qualitative interviews exploring retrospective experiences of growing up with JIA and chronic pain.
Abstract describes a study on meningococcal antibodies, completely mismatched with title. Not relevant.
Qualitative phenomenological study exploring chronic pain experiences in adolescents/young adults with cerebral palsy.
Qualitative case study exploring family management and experiences of an adolescent with SCD and chronic pain.
Quantitative survey study, not qualitative.
Qualitative interviews with adolescents with chronic illnesses including pain conditions (SCD, JRA) exploring transition experiences.
Abstract describes a survey on palliative care program structure, mismatched with title. Not relevant.
Focuses on young women (likely adults) with endometriosis. Unclear pediatric focus.
Qualitative ethnographic study exploring everyday life and coping of children with juvenile arthritis and chronic pain.
Qualitative analysis of social media posts by adolescents with SJIA exploring disease and pain experiences.
Qualitative focus groups exploring peer influences on adolescents' pain experiences and behaviors.
Methodological paper comparing types of qualitative studies in reviews.
Qualitative interviews exploring OTC pain medication use and decision-making in adolescents with chronic pain.
Psychometric validation study, quantitative.
Cochrane review, not primary qualitative research.
Qualitative interviews with children and parents exploring symptoms including abdominal pain and impacts of UC.
Focuses on Duchenne muscular dystrophy, not chronic non-cancer pain.
Conducted in a cancer hospital; review excludes cancer pain.
Clinical review/educational paper, not primary qualitative research.
Qualitative interviews with pediatric patients and parents to develop items including pain intensity and interference for SCD.
Focuses on lifestyle interventions for chronic conditions in primary care, not specifically pediatric chronic pain.
Case report of a single patient. Systematic reviews typically exclude case reports unless specified.
Qualitative interviews exploring lived experiences and treatment perceptions in young people aged 10-13 with JIA.
Curriculum content review, not primary qualitative research on patient experiences.
Cochrane review, not primary qualitative research.
Focuses on acute/procedural pain in hospital settings, not chronic non-cancer pain.
Qualitative interviews exploring social impact and friendship challenges in adolescents with chronic pain.
Focuses on TMD sufferers, likely adults. Unclear pediatric focus.
Quantitative economic/cost-of-illness study.
Bibliographic review on informal care burden, not pediatric chronic pain.
Qualitative study exploring impacts of musculoskeletal impairments including pain in children.
Mixed-methods study including qualitative data on pandemic impact on youth with chronic pain.
Focuses on community nursing services for complex conditions broadly, not specifically chronic pain.
Qualitative thematic analysis exploring experiences of young people with SCD at school, including pain management challenges.
Quantitative study using questionnaires and statistical analyses.
Epidemiological cross-sectional study, quantitative.
Focuses on acute pain experiences in hospitalized vs non-hospitalized children. Quantitative analysis of responses.
Qualitative evidence synthesis on maternity care, not pediatric chronic pain.
Educational/review paper on pain management, not primary qualitative research.
Review article on pain physiology and treatment in critical care.
Qualitative study exploring family experiences and routes to diagnosis for children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
Qualitative interviews exploring symptoms including abdominal pain and impacts in pediatric/adolescent Crohn's disease.
Qualitative interviews and focus groups with parents and staff exploring care improvements for children with SCD, including pain management.
Qualitative interviews including adolescents aged 12-17 with UC exploring symptoms and quality of life impacts including pain.
Qualitative interviews with adolescents aged 15-19 exploring TMD pain experiences and management strategies.
Ethnographic study exploring treatment experiences of youngsters aged 8-18 with functional somatic symptoms at a pain clinic.
Methodological review on meta-ethnography conduct.
Mixed-methods pilot study including qualitative feedback on pain and anxiety management in children/young adults with IBD.
Methodological guidelines paper.
Qualitative interviews and focus groups exploring consequences of non-specific spinal pain in children aged 9-12.
Qualitative focus groups/interviews with adolescents with JIA and caregivers exploring care experiences and service delivery.
Qualitative interviews exploring pain self-management perspectives in adolescents living with HIV.
Qualitative interviews exploring impact of JIA including pain, fatigue, and social aspects in adolescents/young adults.
Focuses on women with dysmenorrhea, likely adults. Unclear pediatric focus.
Qualitative evaluation of a mindfulness intervention for adolescent females with chronic pain.
Qualitative ethnographic study exploring pain expression and care-seeking in Mi'kmaq children and youth.
Methodological evaluation of meta-ethnography as a synthesis method.
Qualitative user-centered design study exploring app acceptability for self-management in young people with JIA.
Qualitative study exploring future narratives and coping with CRPS in adolescents/young adults.
Qualitative interviews exploring transition experiences from pediatric to adult care for young adults with chronic pain.
Feasibility study with qualitative components exploring adaptation of an intervention for parents of youth with chronic pain.
Qualitative metasynthesis/review, not primary qualitative research.
Analyzes published narratives of parent-carers, not primary research on pediatric chronic pain experiences.
Qualitative interviews exploring acceptability of a pain management decision aid for youth with JIA.
Cochrane review, not primary qualitative research.
Qualitative interviews exploring pain experiences and impacts in children with CFS/ME.

Qualitative study examining parents' experiences coping with caring for a child with sickle cell disorder or thalassaemia. Sickle cell disease involves chronic pain (vaso-occlusive crises). Study focuses on parents' experiences and views of service provision, which aligns with review criteria on families' experiences of services.

Scoping review using qualitative content analysis of YouTube videos and viewer comments from adolescents with chronic pain. Explores adolescents' experiences of social support, impact of pain on daily life, and treatment discussions. Meets criteria for qualitative research on adolescents with chronic pain.

Population-based study examining premature deaths in people with intellectual disabilities. Does not focus on children with chronic non-cancer pain or their experiences/perceptions of pain, treatments, or services. Wrong population and research focus.

Qualitative study of adolescents with frequent pain and high OTC analgesic use. However, abstract explicitly states 'Candidate participants were excluded if they were medically diagnosed with an acute or chronic illness, requiring extended use of over-the-counter analgesics within the last year.' Therefore, participants do not have chronic pain as defined by the review criteria.

Mixed methods study including qualitative interviews with 12 adolescents (aged 10-18) and their parents waiting for pediatric chronic pain clinic evaluation. Explores families' experiences of waiting for pain services, which directly addresses review questions about families' views of health and social care services.

Ethnographic qualitative research on adolescent transitioning programs for sickle cell disease patients. SCD involves chronic pain. Study explores adolescents' experiences with healthcare services, patient education, and communication with medical professionals, relevant to review questions about services.

Cross-sectional descriptive study using the Children's Pain Perspectives Inventory applied to 180 HEALTHY Spanish children. Participants do not have chronic pain. Study examines developmental progression of pain perspectives in healthy children, not children with chronic non-cancer pain.

Qualitative semistructured interviews with 25 adolescents aged 15-16 exploring experiences with pain, pain management, and involvement of family and friends. While not explicitly stating all participants have chronic pain, the study examines adolescents' pain experiences and coping strategies in daily life, which may include chronic pain. Conservative inclusion.

Qualitative study analyzing pain narratives of 46 parents of youth with chronic pain recorded during clinical trial baseline sessions. Explores parents' experiences and perspectives of their child's chronic pain, directly addressing review questions about families' conceptualization of chronic pain.

Qualitative study of 102 parents of children with chronic illness (not specifically chronic pain). Focuses on provider behaviors and working relationships. While relevant to service experiences, the population is children with chronic illness broadly, not specifically chronic non-cancer pain.

Qualitative study where children with sickle cell disease were interviewed about their pain experience during vaso-occlusive painful episodes. Explores children's descriptions of pain onset, characteristics, and evolution. SCD involves chronic/recurrent pain, and study captures children's pain perspectives.

Mixed methods study including qualitative interviews with 8 mothers of children with CFS/ME. CFS/ME involves chronic pain and fatigue. Study explores mothers' experiences, concerns about child's distress, and impact on family, relevant to review questions about families' experiences.

Mixed methods study including 8 focus group discussions with caregivers of children with SCD. Explores caregivers' perceptions of socio-behavioral and environmental influences on hospitalization for pain. SCD involves chronic pain, and study captures family perspectives on pain management.

Qualitative study exploring experiences of young adult peer MENTORS (not the adolescents with chronic illness themselves). While some mentors had chronic pain, the study focuses on mentors' experiences of providing support, not on children with chronic pain and their families' experiences.

Qualitative case study of a 14-year-old girl with chronic pain and probable enthesitis-related JIA. Explores her experiences with pain, psychological impact, and art therapy intervention. Captures adolescent's perspective on living with chronic pain and treatment experiences.

Qualitative study with individual and focus group interviews with 36 adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis. JIA involves chronic pain. Explores adolescents' self-management needs, experiences with healthcare providers, pain management strategies, and social support needs.

Qualitative grounded theory study with longitudinal interviews of 8 parents of 4 children with hemophilia. Hemophilia involves bleeding episodes with pain. Explores parents' learning processes, illness management experiences, and interactions with healthcare professionals, relevant to family experiences of services.

Qualitative study with semistructured interviews of 17 adolescents aged 14-19 with chronic tension-type headache. Explores adolescents' coping strategies for managing chronic pain in everyday life, directly addressing review questions about how children live with chronic pain.

Qualitative study of 13 mothers of children with spina bifida. Spina bifida is a neurological disability, not primarily a chronic pain condition. Study focuses on mothers' experiences of parenting children with disabilities, not specifically on chronic pain experiences.

Methodological guidance paper describing the GRADE-CERQual approach for assessing confidence in qualitative evidence syntheses. Not primary research on children with chronic pain. Wrong study type and topic.

Service evaluation of a multidisciplinary outpatient paediatric pain service including qualitative elements from patient questionnaires about their experiences. Explores patients' views of the service, communication with staff, and satisfaction with chronic pain management services.

Qualitative study with in-depth semistructured interviews with 16 families of children with JIA. JIA involves chronic pain. Explores parents' experiences of treatment regimens, medications, exercises, and impact on family roles and relationships, directly addressing review questions.
Quantitative longitudinal study testing a stress and coping model using questionnaires with 159 married couples. Not qualitative research. Study design does not meet inclusion criteria.

Quantitative study using questionnaires and online diary with 60 youth with IBD and parents. While IBD involves pain, the study design is quantitative, not qualitative. Does not meet study design criteria.

Grounded theory and narrative analysis of in-depth semistructured interviews with 53 children ages 10-17 presenting with recurrent pain to a university-based pain clinic. Explores children's experiences of chronic pain, impact on their lives, and treatment outcomes. Directly addresses review questions.
Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial. Not a completed study with results. Protocols are excluded as they do not provide findings on experiences or perceptions.

Qualitative study with in-depth interviews and drawing tasks with 16 children aged 8-12, including 8 children with persistent pain. Explores children's concept of pain, experiences, and communication of pain. Includes children with chronic/persistent pain.

Qualitative descriptive study with semistructured interviews of 13 parents from a pediatric chronic pain clinic. Explores parents' emotional journey, impact on family, and importance of social support. Directly addresses review questions about families' experiences.

Mixed methods study including qualitative interviews with 48 adolescents with SCD and 42 parents. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores religious/spiritual coping strategies used by adolescents and parents, relevant to understanding how families cope with chronic pain.

Qualitative study about mothers of teenage boys with chronic illness. Focuses on chronic illness broadly, not specifically chronic pain. Study develops concept of 'alert assistant' for chronic illness management, not pain-specific.

Qualitative study of 15 parents of children with various disabilities. Broad disability focus, not specifically chronic pain. Study examines life management strategies for parenting children with disabilities generally.

Qualitative study of 11 patients with chronic low back pain. Does not specify age of participants, but context suggests adult population. Study focuses on psychosocial consequences of MRI diagnosis in Saudi Arabia, likely adults.

Qualitative interview study using IPA with 4 young persons and 4 parents who participated in ACT for pediatric chronic pain. Explores lived experiences of treatment, pain education, values-based work, and communication around pain. Directly addresses review questions.

Qualitative study using observation, drawing, role-playing, story-telling, and group discussions with 49 children aged 4-18 experiencing illness and pain. Explores children's perceptions and experiences of pain, directly addressing review questions about how children conceptualize chronic pain.

Ethnographic qualitative study of families of children with JIA. Explores families' perspectives on prescribed exercises, splinting, and medication programs. JIA involves chronic pain. Addresses review questions about families' experiences of treatments and services.

Qualitative phenomenological study with semi-structured interviews and visual aids with 10 adolescents aged 13-17 with JIA or chronic idiopathic pain syndromes. Explores lived experience of pain flares, management strategies, and impact on daily life. Directly addresses review questions.

Qualitative grounded theory study of 46 families of children with JIA. Explores experiences of children with JIA, siblings, mothers, fathers, and grandparents. JIA involves chronic pain. Addresses review questions about families' experiences.

Qualitative study with interviews of 80 participants aged 7-19 with IBD. IBD involves chronic abdominal pain. Explores lived experience, quality of life, coping strategies, and support from family and friends. Addresses review questions about how children live with chronic pain.

Qualitative descriptive study with semistructured interviews of 19 adolescents aged 12-19 with SCD, 2 parents, and 17 healthcare providers. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores adolescents' experiences, self-management challenges, and needs for transitional care services.

Qualitative focus groups with parents of children with medically complex needs. Broad focus on medically complex conditions, not specifically chronic pain. Study examines general care needs, information needs, and support services.

Qualitative photovoice pilot study with youth living with SCD. SCD's primary symptom is severe pain. Explores youth's lived experiences with SCD, coping with the disease, and importance of family and support. Addresses review questions about children's experiences.

Quantitative study with self-reported data, school records, and teacher ratings from 220 adolescents aged 12-17 with chronic pain. Study design is quantitative, not qualitative. Does not meet study design criteria.

Qualitative study with semistructured interviews and art drawing exercises with 19 children with SCD (average age 8.05 years). SCD involves chronic pain. Explores children's religious coping strategies and how they view God/Higher Power in relation to their SCD.

Mixed methods study of 374 young people with type 1 diabetes, cerebral palsy, or autism spectrum disorder. These conditions are not primarily chronic pain conditions. Study focuses on healthcare transition services, not chronic pain experiences.

Qualitative study of adolescents with SCD exploring their experiences of living with the disease including pain, hospital visits, restrictions, and stigma. SCD involves chronic pain. Addresses review questions about how adolescents live with chronic pain.

Qualitative study using consumer engagement framework with interviews of young people aged 10-14 with chronic pain. Explores co-creation of mHealth app for chronic pain management. Addresses review questions about children's experiences and views of treatments.

Qualitative systematic review synthesizing 10 primary studies. While topic is relevant, this is a review/synthesis, not primary qualitative research. Selection criteria specify primary qualitative research.

Modified Delphi study including qualitative data from round 1 with 93 children with chronic pain, 90 parents, and 52 healthcare providers. Explores stakeholders' perspectives on clinically meaningful outcomes for pediatric chronic pain. Includes children's and parents' views on pain management.
Methodological guidance paper from Cochrane on methods for qualitative evidence synthesis. Not primary research on children with chronic pain. Wrong study type.
Mixed method systematic review synthesizing 14 studies. While topic is relevant, this is a review, not primary qualitative research. Does not meet study design criteria.

Abstract describes developing a video instrument for experimental induction of weight stigma in ADULT MEN (18-52 years). Title does not match abstract content. Study population is adults, not children. Wrong population and topic.
Evaluation study using surveys from 31 parents at end of retreat session. Primarily quantitative survey-based evaluation. Does not appear to include qualitative methods for exploring experiences.
Cross-sectional study examining pain teaching in medical school curricula across 15 European countries. Focuses on medical education, not children with chronic pain or their families' experiences.

Qualitative usability testing with semistructured interviews using 'thinking aloud' approach with 20 adolescents with JIA across two iterative cycles. JIA involves chronic pain. Explores adolescents' experiences using electronic pain diary and their perspectives on pain communication.

Qualitative study using IPA with 4 focus groups of 17 parents/carers of adolescents with chronic pain from two UK tertiary clinic sites. Explores parental experiences of caring for adolescent with chronic pain, directly addressing review questions about families' experiences.

Qualitative study with 11 focus groups and 5 semistructured interviews including 21 AYA-SCD, 17 caregivers, and providers. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores transition experiences, pain control beliefs and practices, and patient experiences in healthcare settings.

Qualitative study using IPA with semistructured interviews of 10 caregivers (all mothers) of children aged 5-15 with CP and chronic pain (>3 months). Explores caregivers' experiences of managing child's chronic pain within family, school, and healthcare contexts.

Mixed methods study of 134 parents and 20 service providers of children with life-threatening or chronic conditions requiring complex care. Focuses on palliative and supportive care needs broadly, not specifically chronic non-cancer pain experiences.

Qualitative interview study with 16 parents of children with functional disorders. Functional disorders in children often include chronic pain conditions (functional abdominal pain, functional neurological disorder with pain). Explores parental challenges, emotional experiences, and treatment adherence. Conservative inclusion given overlap with chronic pain.

Quantitative survey study of 123 respondents with cystic fibrosis. Uses questionnaires with open-ended and close-ended questions. Primarily quantitative design examining symptom frequency and self-management. Not qualitative research.

Quantitative epidemiological study using the Luebeck Pain-Screening Questionnaire with 749 children and adolescents. Cross-sectional survey design examining prevalence, characteristics, and consequences of pain. Not qualitative research.

Mixed methods study including semi-structured qualitative interviews with 17 families of children with functional abdominal pain. FAP is a chronic pain condition. Explores families' experiences with the intervention, coping strategies, and perspectives on pain management.

Qualitative study with interviews of 12 children aged 7-11 with JIA. JIA involves chronic pain. Explores children's perceptions of play and leisure, barriers to engagement, and coping strategies. Addresses review questions about how children live with chronic pain.

Qualitative study with semistructured interviews of 31 patients age 5+, 17 parents of patients aged 5-17, and 8 clinicians. Pain is identified as one of the most frequently reported concerns. NF1 with pNF can involve chronic pain. Includes children's and parents' perspectives.

Qualitative study using IPA with 11 participants aged 10-14 with EBS. Abstract describes EBS as a 'chronic, painful and visible skin condition.' Explores young people's experiences of negative treatment, exclusion, and sense of being different. Addresses review questions.
Systematic review and thematic synthesis of 27 qualitative studies. While topic is highly relevant, this is a review/synthesis, not primary qualitative research. Does not meet study design criteria.

Consensus practice guidelines document developed by multidisciplinary group. Not primary research. Provides recommendations for pain assessment in children with SCD, but does not present original qualitative findings.

Qualitative phenomenological study with semistructured interviews of 6 young women aged 16-19 with rheumatological illness. Explores their experiences learning about their illness, communication needs, and preferred learning options. Rheumatological illnesses involve chronic pain.

Mixed methods study with quantitative data from 179 chronic pain patients aged 11-19 and qualitative interviews with 34 mothers and children analyzed using grounded theory. Explores parent-child pain relationships and family dynamics in pediatric chronic pain.

Qualitative study using pain workshop with guided activities and focus group with young people with chronic pain. Explores how chronic pain impacts young people's lives, their experiences, and perspectives. Directly addresses review questions.

Systematic review summarizing 16 studies investigating relationships among family functioning, pain, and pain-related disability. While topic is relevant, this is a review, not primary qualitative research.

Qualitative study with in-depth interviews of 14 caregivers of children with SCD. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores caregivers' knowledge, recognition of complications, and home management strategies including pain management. Addresses review questions about families' experiences.

Qualitative study with 10 interviews of children and adolescents aged 12-18 with SCD. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores barriers to medication adherence, beliefs about medication, and self-management experiences. Addresses review questions about treatments.

Qualitative study with individual interviews of 8 adolescents aged 14-16 and their mothers, analyzed as dyads. Adolescents self-report at least weekly use of analgesics and have frequent pain. Explores pain experiences, family dynamics, and identity development. Conservative inclusion given focus on adolescents with frequent pain.

Mixed methods study with qualitative interviews of 8 mothers of children with profound cognitive impairment who experience frequent and persistent pain. Explores mothers' experiences of assessing and managing their child's pain, developing knowledge and skills. Addresses review questions about families' experiences.

Mixed methods study with 43 children aged 5-16 with JIA including semistructured interviews with children and caregivers. JIA involves chronic pain. Explores children's experiences communicating pain and their preferences for pain assessment tools.

Qualitative study using IPA with telephone interviews of 10 mothers of children with Down's arthritis. Down's arthritis is an aggressive, erosive form of arthritis involving chronic pain. Explores parental experiences, challenges with child pain, and accessing healthcare services.

Qualitative community-based participatory action study with 42 youth aged 8-17 from First Nation communities using Talking Circle and painting workshop. Explores youth's perspectives of physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual pain, and coping strategies. Addresses review questions about children's pain experiences.
Qualitative focus groups with pediatric oncology nurses and physicians about managing children's CANCER pain. Selection criteria specify chronic NON-CANCER pain. Cancer pain is explicitly excluded.
Methodological paper describing purposive sampling framework for qualitative evidence synthesis on vaccination communication. Not about chronic pain. Wrong topic and study type.

Qualitative study with iterative cycles of in-depth cognitive interviews with adolescents and young adults with SCD. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores their experiences with pain and perspectives on pain diary design. Addresses review questions about children's views.

Qualitative study with 32 semistructured individual and 2 focus-group interviews with children and adolescents aged 8-17 with chronic/recurrent pain, plus 32 interviews with parents. Explores children's and parents' perspectives on pain outcomes and measurement. Directly addresses review questions.

Qualitative study with thematic analysis of interviews with 25 pediatric patients aged 10-17 with IBD. IBD involves chronic abdominal pain. Explores children's and adolescents' illness experiences and challenges. Addresses review questions about how children live with chronic pain.

Quantitative cross-sectional study with 194 adolescents aged 12-18 using questionnaires and pain diary. Examines relationships between pain characteristics, psychosocial factors, and quality of life. Study design is quantitative, not qualitative.

Qualitative study with interviews of 15 nurses about their experiences providing nonpharmacological pain management in palliative care. Focuses on healthcare providers' experiences, not children with chronic pain or their families. Wrong population.

Cognitive interviews with 44 people with CRPS to examine content validity of a patient-reported outcome measure. Does not specify age, but context suggests adult population. Study focuses on instrument validation, not experiences of children with chronic pain.

Narrative review plus qualitative focus group with 4 adolescent females with chronic pain. Explores pain-related stigma from medical providers, school personnel, peers, and family members. Includes primary qualitative data from adolescents with chronic pain.

Qualitative multiple case study with 5 adolescents who underwent HCT for SCD, including patient interviews, parent interviews, and medical record analysis. SCD involves chronic pain. Explores adolescents' and parents' experiences of quality of life, including pain, social isolation, and psychological stress.

Mixed methods study with 14 females aged 13-19 with childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus including semistructured interviews about intervention experiences. Lupus involves chronic pain. Explores adolescents' experiences with treatment and symptom management.

Mixed methods study with semistructured interviews of 28 adolescent girls with dysmenorrhea. Dysmenorrhea involves recurrent/chronic menstrual pain. Explores girls' self-care strategies, symptom management, and communication about pain. Addresses review questions about adolescents' pain experiences.

Qualitative play interviews with children with chronic illnesses and their siblings. Broad chronic illness focus, not specifically chronic pain. Study examines perceptions of hospitalization and medical procedures, not chronic pain experiences specifically.

Qualitative study analyzing written narratives from 39 families (children and parents separately) with functional abdominal pain. FAP is a chronic pain condition. Explores families' experiences of pain characteristics, triggers, consequences, coping strategies, and diagnostic process.

Commentary/opinion piece discussing systemic racism in chronic noncancer pain management. Not primary research. Provides historical context and commentary on racial injustice in medicine, but does not present original qualitative findings from children or families.

Mixed methods study with 128 adolescents meeting ICD-11 criteria for chronic pain, including qualitative interviews explaining quantitative findings. Explores adolescents' pain management strategies (physical, psychological, interpersonal). Addresses review questions about adolescents' experiences.

Retrospective semistructured telephone interviews with 24 former patients (mean age 15.63 years) and parents from Complex Pain Consultation Service. Includes qualitative information about treatment experiences, pain management strategies, and satisfaction with interdisciplinary care.

Qualitative study with individual semistructured interviews (n=10) and 3 focus groups with parents of children aged 4-12 with Marfan syndrome. Parents report children experience fatigue, pain, and physical impairments. Explores parents' perspectives on daily functioning and disease burden.

Qualitative study with 17 parent caregivers of children with medical complexity during PICU admission. Focuses on medical complexity and acute hospitalization experiences, not specifically chronic non-cancer pain. Wrong focus.

Mixed methods pilot feasibility study with 8 children aged 4-8 with JIA including qualitative thematic analysis of open-ended questions from parents, teachers, therapists, and children. JIA involves chronic pain. Explores experiences using booklet for pain and fatigue management at school.

Qualitative essay based on oral history responses of 32 patients with chronic pain at Pediatric Pain Clinic at UCLA. Explores children's experiences with pain, family dynamics, coping strategies, and understanding of pain. Captures children's perspectives on living with chronic pain.

Qualitative content analysis of semistructured interviews with 21 adolescents aged 15-19 with TMD pain. Explores adolescents' experiences of living with recurrent TMD pain, impact on daily life, and emotional responses. Directly addresses review questions.

Qualitative study with children aged 3-12 years with sickle cell anemia (chronic pain condition). Uses Grounded Theory methodology with interviews and therapeutic play sessions. Explores children's experiences of pain, suffering, and treatment. Meets all inclusion criteria.

While the population (young people 12-16 years with sickle cell disease) is appropriate, the study design is cross-sectional using semistructured questionnaires, which is quantitative rather than qualitative. Does not meet the qualitative research requirement.

Mixed-methods study with adolescents and parents regarding chronic pain management. Contains qualitative component (qualitative results mentioned) exploring needs and experiences with chronic pain services. Conservative inclusion due to mixed methods design.

This is a classification system development paper, not primary qualitative research. It describes ICD-11 coding proposals for chronic pain but does not report empirical qualitative findings from children or families.

Qualitative study with adolescents and young adults living with chronic pain. Uses focus groups and thematic analysis to explore sources of joy and pain experiences. While 'young adults' may exceed age 18, conservative inclusion given pediatric pain focus.

Qualitative study with adolescents 11-17 years with CFS/ME (chronic condition with pain symptoms). Semi-structured interviews with adolescents, parents, and HCPs exploring treatment acceptability and barriers to recovery. Meets inclusion criteria.

While qualitative and involving adolescents, the focus is on kidney transplantation information needs, not chronic pain experiences. Pain is mentioned as one of four stressors but is not the primary focus of the study.

Qualitative study with parent-adolescent dyads where adolescents have JIA or Crohn's disease (conditions involving chronic pain). Explores treatment decision factors and quality of life considerations. Conservative inclusion as pain is relevant to these conditions.

Qualitative study with children 10-18 years and their caregivers focusing on long-term pain after surgery. Explores family experiences of pain, recovery challenges, and intervention preferences. Directly addresses chronic pain experiences.

Mixed-methods study with children 10-18 years with chronic pain at a tertiary clinic. Includes qualitative semistructured interviews analyzing functioning patterns and coping strategies. Strong fit for inclusion criteria.
This is a Cochrane Review (systematic review), not primary qualitative research. The abstract only contains background information without reporting qualitative findings from children or families.

Qualitative study with pediatric patients, parents, and healthcare professionals about chronic pain treatment aftercare. Uses reflexive thematic analysis to explore treatment experiences and mechanisms. Meets all inclusion criteria.

Qualitative study with youth 13-20 years with chronic pain and their parents during COVID-19. While some participants may be over 18, the majority appear to be adolescents. Explores lived experiences of pain management and care access.

While qualitative and about chronic non-cancer pain, the study appears to focus on adult patients (recruited from Ramathibodi Hospital Pain Clinic). No indication that children 3 months-18 years were included.

Qualitative study with children 6-11 years with JIA (chronic inflammatory arthritis with pain). Uses art therapy techniques to identify research priorities around symptoms, side effects, and pain management. Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a methodological guidance paper for meta-ethnography reporting, not primary qualitative research about children with chronic pain. Does not meet any inclusion criteria.

Quantitative study using diaries and questionnaires with adolescents 12-18 years. While the population and topic are appropriate, the study design is not qualitative (no interviews, focus groups, or qualitative analysis).

Qualitative ethnographic study with children 5-12 years with cystic fibrosis (chronic condition with pain symptoms). Uses grounded theory with interviews and drawings. Conservative inclusion as CF involves chronic pain experiences.

While qualitative and involving families of children with chronic illness, the focus is on fathers' emotional impact of caregiving, not on children's or families' experiences/perceptions of chronic pain itself.

Qualitative study with youths 11-15 years with functional disorders (often presenting with unexplained pain) and their parents. Uses interpretative phenomenological analysis to explore illness perceptions. Conservative inclusion as functional disorders commonly involve pain symptoms.
